description: Controlled vocabulary defining canonical outcomes produced by diagnostic actions, tests, corrective actions, validation steps, and completed A.R.I.A. cases.

outcome_types.name: HYPOTHESIS_SUPPORTED
outcome_types.description: New evidence materially increases support for a hypothesis without yet establishing confirmation.

outcome_types.name: HYPOTHESIS_WEAKENED
outcome_types.description: New evidence materially decreases support for a hypothesis without conclusively ruling it out.

outcome_types.name: HYPOTHESIS_CONFIRMED
outcome_types.description: Available evidence is sufficient to establish the hypothesis as the confirmed diagnosis or failure condition under the applicable confidence policy.

outcome_types.name: HYPOTHESIS_RULED_OUT
outcome_types.description: Available evidence is sufficient to remove the hypothesis from active consideration for the current diagnostic state.

outcome_types.name: HYPOTHESIS_UNCHANGED
outcome_types.description: The resulting evidence does not materially change support for the hypothesis.

outcome_types.name: TEST_POSITIVE
outcome_types.description: A diagnostic test produced the defined positive condition.

outcome_types.name: TEST_NEGATIVE
outcome_types.description: A diagnostic test did not produce the defined positive condition.

outcome_types.name: TEST_INCONCLUSIVE
outcome_types.description: The test was performed but the result does not sufficiently discriminate between relevant hypotheses.

outcome_types.name: FAULT_FOLLOWED_COMPONENT
outcome_types.description: During a controlled component substitution or swap, the abnormal condition moved with the tested component.

outcome_types.name: FAULT_DID_NOT_FOLLOW_COMPONENT
outcome_types.description: During a controlled component substitution or swap, the abnormal condition did not move with the tested component.

outcome_types.name: FAULT_FOLLOWED_PATH
outcome_types.description: During a controlled path change or swap, the abnormal condition moved with the tested physical or logical path.

outcome_types.name: FAULT_DID_NOT_FOLLOW_PATH
outcome_types.description: During a controlled path change or swap, the abnormal condition did not move with the tested physical or logical path.

outcome_types.name: ACTION_COMPLETED
outcome_types.description: The requested or selected action was successfully performed.

outcome_types.name: ACTION_PARTIALLY_COMPLETED
outcome_types.description: Only part of the requested or selected action could be completed.

outcome_types.name: ACTION_NOT_PERFORMED
outcome_types.description: The requested or selected action was not performed.

outcome_types.name: ACTION_UNABLE_TO_PERFORM
outcome_types.description: The action could not be performed because of access, equipment, permissions, safety, environmental, operational, or other constraints.

outcome_types.name: ACTION_REFUSED
outcome_types.description: The person responsible for execution explicitly declined to perform the requested action.

outcome_types.name: ACTION_DEFERRED
outcome_types.description: The action was intentionally postponed for later execution.

outcome_types.name: ACTION_BLOCKED_BY_SAFETY
outcome_types.description: The action was not performed because an applicable safety requirement or condition prevented execution.

outcome_types.name: ACTION_BLOCKED_BY_SERVICE_IMPACT
outcome_types.description: The action was not performed because the expected or possible service impact was not acceptable or authorized.

outcome_types.name: CONDITION_IMPROVED
outcome_types.description: The relevant technical condition improved after an action or over the observation interval but has not necessarily returned to acceptable condition.

outcome_types.name: CONDITION_UNCHANGED
outcome_types.description: No material change was observed in the relevant technical condition.

outcome_types.name: CONDITION_WORSENED
outcome_types.description: The relevant technical condition became materially worse.

outcome_types.name: SYMPTOM_ELIMINATED
outcome_types.description: A previously observed symptom is no longer present following an action or change.

outcome_types.name: SYMPTOM_PERSISTS
outcome_types.description: The original symptom remains present after the relevant action, test, or observation period.

outcome_types.name: NEW_SYMPTOM_OBSERVED
outcome_types.description: A previously unrecorded symptom appeared during diagnosis, testing, or corrective work.

outcome_types.name: CORRECTION_SUCCESSFUL
outcome_types.description: A corrective action produced the predicted technical correction and subsequent validation supports success.

outcome_types.name: CORRECTION_PARTIALLY_SUCCESSFUL
outcome_types.description: A corrective action improved the condition but did not fully restore the required technical state.

outcome_types.name: CORRECTION_UNSUCCESSFUL
outcome_types.description: A corrective action failed to produce the predicted technical improvement or resolution.

outcome_types.name: VALIDATION_PASSED
outcome_types.description: Post-action validation satisfies the applicable success criteria.

outcome_types.name: VALIDATION_FAILED
outcome_types.description: Post-action validation does not satisfy the applicable success criteria.

outcome_types.name: VALIDATION_INCOMPLETE
outcome_types.description: Available post-action evidence is insufficient to determine whether the applicable success criteria were satisfied.

outcome_types.name: CASE_RESOLVED
outcome_types.description: The reported technical problem has been resolved and sufficient validation supports closure.

outcome_types.name: CASE_PARTIALLY_RESOLVED
outcome_types.description: A meaningful portion of the technical problem was corrected but one or more relevant conditions remain unresolved.

outcome_types.name: CASE_UNRESOLVED
outcome_types.description: The case ended or paused without resolving the reported technical problem.

outcome_types.name: CASE_ESCALATED
outcome_types.description: Further resolution responsibility was transferred or escalated because continued diagnosis required additional authority, expertise, access, resources, or information.

outcome_types.name: CASE_ABANDONED
outcome_types.description: Diagnostic work stopped without resolution or formal escalation.

outcome_types.name: CASE_DUPLICATE
outcome_types.description: The case was determined to represent the same underlying incident as another recorded case.

outcome_types.name: NO_FAULT_FOUND
outcome_types.description: Sufficient investigation was performed but the reported abnormal condition could not be reproduced or validated.

outcome_types.name: EXTERNAL_CAUSE
outcome_types.description: The reported condition was determined to originate outside the microwave system or diagnostic responsibility represented by the case.

outcome_types.name: CASE_REOPENED
outcome_types.description: A previously resolved or closed case became active again because the original or materially related condition returned.

outcome_types.name: RECURRENCE_CONFIRMED
outcome_types.description: A previously resolved technical condition has been confirmed to have recurred.

outcome_types.name: LEARNING_ELIGIBLE
outcome_types.description: Case evidence and outcome quality are sufficient for the case to contribute to ARIA's learned diagnostic experience.

outcome_types.name: LEARNING_RESTRICTED
outcome_types.description: The case may contribute only limited learning because diagnosis, evidence quality, applicability, validation, or outcome certainty is incomplete.

outcome_types.name: LEARNING_EXCLUDED
outcome_types.description: The case shall not modify learned diagnostic probability or route-performance statistics.

outcome_types.name: OUTCOME_UNKNOWN
outcome_types.description: Available information is insufficient to classify the outcome.

semantic_rules.rule: Completion of an action and technical success of an action are separate outcomes. ACTION_COMPLETED shall not imply CORRECTION_SUCCESSFUL.
Improvement does not independently establish resolution. CONDITION_IMPROVED shall remain distinct from SYMPTOM_ELIMINATED, VALIDATION_PASSED, and CASE_RESOLVED.
A hypothesis may be supported or weakened without being confirmed or ruled out.
A corrective action that produces no predicted change shall generate new diagnostic evidence and shall trigger reevaluation of affected hypotheses.
A corrective action producing the predicted change may support causation, but ARIA shall consider whether the action changed multiple variables before assigning causal confidence.
A case shall not be marked CASE_RESOLVED solely because a corrective action was performed. Resolution requires sufficient validation that the reported condition is corrected.
Inconclusive, incomplete, unavailable, refused, or blocked actions shall not be interpreted as negative diagnostic results unless the missing result itself has established diagnostic significance.
ARIA shall distinguish between a hypothesis being ruled out by evidence and a hypothesis merely becoming less probable.
Historical learning shall distinguish successful diagnostic routes from merely completed diagnostic routes.
Cases with uncertain root cause or insufficient validation shall not contribute to learned causal probability with the same weight as validated resolved cases.
A reopened or recurrent case shall retain linkage to the prior case and its previous diagnosis, corrective action, validation, and elapsed time to recurrence.
Learning eligibility shall be evaluated separately from case closure. A closed case is not automatically a trustworthy learning example.
Isolation-test outcomes shall identify the controlled variable and shall not be generalized to unrelated components, products, or contexts without supporting evidence.
ARIA shall preserve unsuccessful diagnostic actions because failed routes contain information useful for future route optimization.
Outcome classifications shall describe what actually occurred rather than what ARIA predicted would occur.
